subject: Tenor & price-sensitivity: request for price protection on reserved GPU lanes
messages:
From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@heliohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity — price protection ask

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the thorough demo last week. As we finalize commercials for the 24-month reserved GPU commitment, Procurement has one open ask that is blocking legal: market-price protection. Given the volatility in GPU spot and OEM pricing we've seen, Helio needs a mechanism to avoid overpaying if market rates fall materially mid-tenor.

Specifically our procurement team asked whether Redwood can offer either:
- a rebate if the 6-month trailing market index falls >20% vs. the signed price, OR
- a price collar with an upside cap and a rebate floor (we'd accept a small annual premium for stability).

We understand this affects your exposure. Our target: finalize contract terms and PO by 2027-10-28. Can you outline what guardrails Redwood would need (limit on rebate %, lookback window, activation triggers) and any approvals required?

Attached: Helio_RFP_Q4_2027.pdf (procurement worksheet).

Appreciate a quick note on feasibility — Sam
Sam Reed
Head of Procurement, Helio Health
Sam.Reed@heliohealth.com
phone +1 415-555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reed <sam.reed@heliohealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity — price protection ask

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can support a limited market-protection construct; below is a pragmatic approach that balances Helio's risk appetite and Redwood's exposure.

Proposed options (high level):
1) Conditional credit (preferred short path):
   - Trigger: 6-month trailing market index for comparable GPU SKU drops >25% vs signed unit price
   - Remedy: one-time billing credit equal to up to 12% of committed monthly spend (capped) applied to next invoice
   - Lookback: single 6-month observation period during the tenor (customer may select the period once)

2) Price collar (longer legal lead time):
   - Customer pays a small premium (2–4% on committed volume) to establish a floor/ceiling mechanism. If market < floor, customer receives rebate; if market > ceil, price stays as signed (no clawback).
   - Collar requires Finance + Legal signoff and a short addendum to the MSA.

Operational guardrails we need:
- Max rebate exposure per deal: 12% of committed spend across tenor
- Approval threshold: any structure that creates >10% expected revenue impact requires Director-level approval (Karthik as pricing approver)
- Credit applies as a billing credit (no retroactive cash refunds)
- Index and calculation method must be agreed in SOW (we propose a 3rd-party GPU market index; provide two vendor choices)

Next steps:
- I attached a proforma (proforma_hl_deal_20271020.xlsx) with scenario math for both options.
- If Helio is comfortable with option 1, we can draft a short amendment and route to DocuSign in 48–72 hours. If they prefer the collar, allow 10 business days for legal + finance review.

Can we book a 30-minute call tomorrow to align?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: proforma_hl_deal_20271020.xlsx (proforma, estimated rebate scenarios)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity — price protection ask

Marissa — good framing. Two quick asks from my side before we commit to option language:
1) What is Helio's expected activation profile across the 24 months? (phased vs. immediate) — that changes exposure materially.
2) Suggest we limit rebate to a single exercise during the tenor (Helio gets one lookback). Otherwise exposure multiplies.

My suggested negotiation anchor (internal):
- Offer: 10% upfront volume discount + conditional credit up to 12% of monthly committed spend if index drops >25% (single exercise, 6-month trailing lookback)
- Require exec approval if the credit mechanics could reduce expected recognized revenue by >10% vs. baseline.

If Karthik is comfortable, I'll send the option 1 amendment to Helio and propose a quick call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity — price protection ask

Forwarding my thoughts after reviewing the proforma. High level sign-off with guardrails below.

On Wed, Oct 20, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> (proposed options and attachments)

Karthik's decision notes:  
- Approve Option 1 pathway (conditional credit) as the default commercial path to keep the deal fast-moving.
- Guardrails we require:  
  * Max credit cap: 12% of committed monthly spend (applies once over tenor)
  * Single exercise only (customer elects the 6-month observation window once)
  * Credit applied as invoice offset; no cash refunds or retroactive recognition adjustments without Finance sign-off
  * Any construct that meaningfully (>=10%) reduces NRR or recognized revenue vs. baseline must be routed to Finance + Exec approvals (Karthik sign-off not sufficient for >10% impact)
  * Legal to confirm index vendor language and dispute process (we prefer vendor A or vendor B — both included in Drive link)

Operational asks for Sales Ops / CS: prepare 3 scenario tables (base, -20% market, -35% market) showing actual dollar exposure and accounting treatment. Naomi, please own the scenario pack and confirm cost-treatment guidance with Finance.

Ben: proceed to propose Option 1 to Helio on a 48–72 hour turnaround. If Helio asks for the price-collar path, shift to Legal and allow for 10 business days. Route any >10% impact constructs to me and the CFO.

I'll approve final amendment language once Legal confirms index verbiage.

Thanks — Karthik
